findings.evidence: deploy/compose.sh uses exec env -i and passes the selected project and Unix endpoint only to its Docker child. Official Compose project precedence recognizes -p, COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, top-level name and directory basename, not SBARBASE_COMPOSE_PROJECT: https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/project-name/. Compose inherits Docker endpoint inputs independently: https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/environment-variables/envvars/. Existing inert launcher test confirms a selected project crosses into the child environment, but no fixture covers the next documented operator command.
findings.impact: An admitted custom deployment cannot complete the documented first-operator journey without undocumented arguments. Observation and cleanup may select an absent or different project or endpoint, defeating the deployment isolation promised by the new launcher.

Raw Compose does not recognize SBARBASE_COMPOSE_PROJECT and instead derives the project from the checkout directory. The same mismatch affects logs, smoke, down and upgrade. Likewise, selecting only SBARBASE_DOCKER_SOCKET does not set DOCKER_HOST in the parent shell, so raw Docker uses its own saved/default endpoint. No actual Docker call was made for this source reproduction.

On a pending applied/rolling_back upgrade, lab/upgrade_guard.py:583-608 takes upgrade and supervisor locks, writes upgrade state and can move the checkout; move_checkout invokes bun_install (lines 298-300 and 409-416). On running owned leftovers, lab/leftover_runtime.py:138 enters probe, whose lines 102-109 create the state directory and lock files before installation_stop. supervise admission at line 638 runs only during render/apply, so it cannot admit every future restart after endpoint or host capability changes. The caller suite passes while test_supervisor_unit.py:51-78 and test_supervised_run.py:61-67 retain assertions that the guard comes first. The legacy service remains a documented installation route and R2 has no exclusion for its startup boundary.
findings.reproduction: Source-only trace: start the shipped or rendered unit on a host whose capability now fails with a pending upgrade state.
